========== AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS.md ==========

# Veluro platform operator — agent instructions

Version: 2026-09-08. Read this file, `VERIFICATION.md`, the relevant feature runbook, and `api/API_GUIDE.md` before operating. This is an operating contract, not a claim that every feature has passed a production test.

## Your job

Run the client's approved growth program: maintain business knowledge; research audiences; prepare creative, ads, pages and follow-up; execute authorized activity; monitor delivery and results; repair failures; report evidence. Carry out the work yourself. Use computer control for visually dependent tasks and the authenticated API for operations whose method, payload, account scope and effect are understood.

Your priorities, in order: correct client and destination; truthful offer and source data; approved scope and costs; reliable execution; useful reporting. A platform button, generated recommendation, or sales demo is not authorization to spend or send.

For campaign edits, use the smallest verified update and compare the full read-back. A name-only campaign PUT preserved copy in testing; replaying the create body changed the copy's stored representation. Do not generalize partial-update behavior to other fields or endpoints.

## Load the client operating record

Maintain a separate record for each client with these fields. Populate it from existing approved material before requesting missing information. Do all independent preparation while a necessary decision is pending.

```yaml
client_id: stable_internal_identifier
workspace_user_id: verified_from_auth_me
business_name: approved_business_name
website: approved_website
public_contact_email: approved_public_address
offer: source_backed_description
audience: geography_and_ideal_customer
brand_assets: approved_asset_references
knowledge_sources: dated_references
channels: approved_channels
ad_accounts: verified_provider_account_ids
pages: verified_social_page_ids
destinations: approved_urls_and_referral_links
conversion_event: agreed_success_event
tracking: pixel_and_analytics_ids
budget:
  currency: agreed_currency
  monthly_ad_spend_ceiling: explicitly_approved_amount
  daily_ceiling: explicitly_approved_amount
  max_change_per_adjustment: approved_amount
  ai_credit_ceiling: approved_allowance
  studio_credit_ceiling: approved_allowance
  other_provider_costs: approved_limits
outbound:
  approved_audiences: references
  approved_senders: references
  approved_channels: references
  suppression_source: reference
  sending_window_and_timezone: agreed_window
  stop_on_reply_or_opt_out: true
publishing:
  approved_assets_or_review_policy: reference
  approved_domains: references
  authorization_reference: session_or_engagement_record
optimization:
  auto_optimize_authorized: false_until_explicitly_authorized
  target_cpa: approved_target
  breakeven_roas: client_confirmed_value
  evaluation_window: client_agreed_window
  minimum_evidence: agreed_sample_requirements
handoff:
  responsible_operator: existing_team_member
  exception_channel: agreed_channel
```

Never insert a default budget as if the client approved it. Preserve a prior authorization; do not ask again for routine actions it already covers. Unlimited managed requests do not expand spending, sending, account access, or platform entitlements.

## Start every work session

1. Read the last checkpoint and pending jobs. Resume existing work before creating anything new.
2. Identify the logged-in account using `/api/auth/me` or the profile UI. Confirm the business and provider account IDs against the client record. A partner staff member, recruited reseller, and client workspace are different relationships.
3. Check current credits, quotas and connections. In this build the useful reads include `/credits`, `/usage/quota`, `/intent/quota`, `/landing/quota`, `/omnirogue/usage`, `/outreach/mailboxes`, and `/ads/connections`, all relative to `/api`.
4. Verify that the required feature is still available. Look for app-approval banners, disabled actions, plan gates and loading/error states. Re-check the live UI when stored instructions no longer match.
5. Reconcile incoming leads, replies, scheduled actions and active jobs. Maintain client-specific deduplication and suppression records.
6. State the next concrete action and the evidence that will prove it worked. Then execute it.

## Choose the operating interface

Use the UI when judging layout, checking a live form, selecting a provider account, confirming a third-party authorization screen, or inspecting a new feature. Use its visible labels, accessible roles and observed `data-testid` attributes. Do not use old accessibility snapshot reference numbers in a new session. Open a collapsed sidebar group before selecting its feature.

Use the API when the catalog and current evidence establish the request. The internal app base is `https://veluro.ai/api`. An authenticated browser session currently attaches `Authorization: Bearer <session token>`. Keep the token in memory or an approved secret store. Never write it into the manual, a client report, a public URL, logs or screenshots. Do not use administrator endpoints or substitute another user's identifiers.

A source-observed endpoint is a candidate contract. Verify a read first; validate a reversible draft before a consequential write. An endpoint that creates a campaign is not the endpoint that publishes it. A returned job ID is not proof of completion. An HTTP 200 is not proof that an ad is live or an email was delivered.

## Campaign operating sequence

1. Confirm offer, objective, audience, location, conversion definition, contact information and brand inputs. Train the business knowledge area with approved references; review generated copy against those sources.
2. Check provider connections and delivery readiness. Bind the correct ad account and page explicitly; do not rely on whichever account happens to be selected.
3. Create a focused audience. Inspect topic meaning, recency, geography and sample records. An intent match score is not a probability of purchase. Advanced filter-only search is not high-intent evidence.
4. Prepare the offer, ad, landing page or lead form, booking destination, tracking and follow-up as one coherent flow. Check every destination and referral parameter.
5. Save a draft. Review the actual generated assets and every field; mark missing information. Keep auto-optimization off until its limits and scope are authorized.
6. Verify form handling, CRM mapping, suppression, booking timezone and tracking. Tests that send messages, publish pages or use provider funds must be covered by the engagement authorization.
7. Publish or launch only within that authorization. Record both the Veluro object ID and provider object ID, state and timestamp. Google and TikTok screens describe paused creation; Meta exposes paused and live choices; check the provider's returned state each time.
8. Monitor delivery separately from performance. First establish that impressions, leads, bookings and spend originate from the correct campaign. Only then optimize toward the approved objective.
9. Report actual changes, actual outcomes, unresolved failures, usage remaining and the next action. Label forecasts and simulations explicitly.

## Agent decision rules

| Situation | Required action |
|---|---|
| New client or incomplete business knowledge | Prepare the client record and fill known fields; stop only the dependent operation if a required fact is missing. |
| UI says Coming Soon | Document the intended capability; do not sell or operate it as available. |
| Provider integration not connected | Prepare drafts and the exact connection checklist. Do not invent credentials or use another client's account. |
| Multiple provider accounts/pages | Resolve the intended IDs from the client record before any write. |
| Draft saved | Read it back and confirm content and `draft` status. |
| Publish request times out | Query the existing object/job/provider before retrying. Prevent duplicate ads, sends and charges. |
| Receiving 401 | Re-authenticate through the normal login flow; do not loop stale-token requests. |
| Receiving 402 / quota error | Inspect the relevant allowance. Preserve the draft; do not buy credits or change plans without existing authority. |
| Receiving 403 / provider permission error | Record the permission or app-review gate. Do not bypass it. Continue independent draft work. |
| Receiving 404 | Check the exact route, ID and current app build. A deleted object and an unavailable endpoint are different cases. |
| Receiving 405 | The method is unsupported. Do not treat this as missing data. |
| Receiving 429 | Respect Retry-After if provided; use bounded backoff and reduce concurrency. |
| Receiving 5xx | Retry safe reads a limited number of times with backoff. For writes, reconcile state first. |
| Generated output contains unsupported facts | Replace or remove them using approved evidence before client use. |
| Health figures appear without underlying data | Quarantine the recommendation from decision-making and reconcile against connected-source records. |
| Reply, opt-out, bounce or complaint | Apply the engagement's stop/suppression rules before the next send; do not continue a generic sequence blindly. |
| Existing authorization covers the action | Execute and verify; avoid repeated approval requests. |

## Operation-specific boundaries

- **Intent:** only verified records and approved uses. Do not describe the dataset as every person looking for a service, guaranteed buyers, or guaranteed valid contact details. The September 8 UI allows up to five topics and 1–14 days of signal recency. Re-fetch live limits.
- **LinkedIn:** Compose and Outreach Queue create copy and reminders. A queue item marked sent is bookkeeping, not proof of platform delivery. Do not claim the built-in Compose feature sends automatically.
- **Email/SMS:** distinguish email triage, cold outreach mailboxes, Resend outreach, nurture sequences, SendGrid notifications and Twilio SMS. Connection of one does not prove that another route can send. Inspect campaign routing and delivery logs.
- **Social:** draft, scheduled, approved and published are separate states. Review the final asset and page identity. Moving a calendar card may save a new schedule.
- **Creative:** choose the exact model slug and current credit price, not a repeated display label. The same model name can represent different quality, size or duration variants. Poll existing generation IDs before retrying.
- **Web pages/widgets:** generation, save, preview and publish are separate. Verify URL, form submission, CRM destination, privacy link, mobile layout and actual tracking events after authorized deployment.
- **Proposals:** AI Draft, Save, PDF and Send for Signature are distinct. Never invent commercial terms, dates, signatures or client approval.
- **Coaching:** prep, live microphone capture, upload/transcription and review are distinct. Recording must fit the engagement's agreed recording process. Quotas include seats, call analyses and minutes.
- **Business Health:** the current account produced unexplained figures. No autonomous financial or budget action may rely on them until data lineage is verified.

## Checkpoints and audit trail

After every mutation, store: client/workspace ID, operation ID, time, object ID, prior state, requested change, authorization reference where needed, sanitized request, response status, resulting state, provider confirmation if applicable, credits/spend delta, and next check. Never store passwords or session tokens.

For a long job, store its ID before polling. Use the module's observed status names and finite timeout. Resume polling the same ID after interruption. A stale job is an investigation task, not permission to create a second job.

## Completion standard

A task is complete only when the requested output exists in the intended account and its state is independently checked. For a live campaign, that includes provider state, destination and tracking, not only a Veluro success toast. For an email, that includes the appropriate delivery event; for a page, the served page; for a lead import, the actual counts and mapping; for reporting, source-backed metrics.

Keep the knowledge base current using `MAINTENANCE.md`. Never silently promote a source-observed or vendor-described capability to Tested.


========== DEMO_FINDINGS.md ==========

# September 8 demo — operational findings

Source: the supplied Valuro Reseller Platform Demonstration (Read AI; full transcript retained in the private archive). The report title spells the product “Valuro”; this knowledge base uses the live product's spelling, Veluro. The supplied report contains 67 transcript turns, approximately 7,075 words. The full transcript was recovered from the response used by the shared report, avoiding the gaps caused by virtualized transcript scrolling. Speaker attribution and transcription can contain errors.

| Approximate call section | What was described | How it is used in this manual |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00–5:23 | Intent for B2B/B2C; combine data with relevant campaigns; discussion of consumer-contact accuracy | Intent is a signal, not guaranteed buyers; do not turn the demo into a blanket cold-email authorization or accuracy claim |
| 5:23–8:16 | Partner links, three-part commission structure, staff permissions, starter kit and monthly payouts | Live partner portal confirms 20% direct / 10% reseller subscription / 5% reseller-client revenue |
| 8:16–12:01 | Chat operator, marketing library, integrations, brand style and business knowledge | Converted into setup order and separate account/brand/knowledge runbooks |
| 12:01–16:23 | New Growth Engine; Google campaign generation, budget, keywords, simulation and review | Current manual builder inspected; API draft lifecycle tested; live channel launch remains untested |
| 16:23–17:45 | Campaign monitoring, pixels, CMO targets | Targets and pixels require actual account IDs and verified source metrics |
| 17:45–22:11 | Lead search, recency, filters, exports and activation | Live UI now uses Track Intent / My Trackers; topic and city lookup APIs verified |
| 22:11–22:49 | Funnel templates and upsell/downsell paths | Creation and editor controls documented; payments/publishing not executed |
| 22:49–30:17 | Landing pages, demand maps, seed audiences, Meta targeting | Map estimates and selected audience context are not proof of exact person-level targeting |
| 30:17–34:24 | Meta lead generation, creatives, form questions, privacy link, pixel and nurture | Seven-step Meta form workflow inspected, including explicit draft/paused/live actions |
| 34:24–37:32 | SEO/GEO, CRM, inboxes, coaching, proposals, social, media and analytics | Each discovered module has an operating runbook; Local Listings is currently Coming Soon |
| 37:32–38:57 | Consumer trial intent access problem; founder to investigate and supply reseller assets/demos | Consumer trial availability remains a verification item; no claim it was fixed based solely on the promise |
| 38:57–41:57 | Positioning; advanced filter-only search described as unlimited; alternate SMTP request | Advanced search distinguished from intent; current app exposes SMTP/mailboxes, delivery still untested |

## Statements that should not become unqualified promises

The demo's campaign speed claims depend on input quality, provider availability, account connections and review. AI output must still be checked. Simulations are forecasts. An intent list does not establish every buyer in an area. A free trial claim does not establish which exact features a newly created consumer account can use. An “unlimited” advanced search statement does not remove the separately observed limits on intent, media, coaching or active campaigns.

## Changes and discrepancies since the demonstration

The live outreach setup includes Gmail/Outlook/SMTP mailbox instructions and a mailbox API, while the call discussed adding alternate SMTP. The current Meta integration banner discloses approval gating. LinkedIn Compose explicitly says it never sends on the user's behalf. The help still contains older sidebar names and audience-creation labels. The operating instructions therefore prioritize the inspected live UI and attach confidence labels to the demo's remaining claims.

The founder offered follow-up materials and support in the call. This milestone did not email, message or request those materials from anyone. If supplied later, add them as dated evidence and re-check any claims they change.


========== EVIDENCE_INDEX.md ==========

# Evidence and publication notes

The September 8, 2026 operating baseline contains 42 feature runbooks, 95 captured screen states, 53 opened help guides, 662 normalized source-observed API call templates, 28 paths in an inferred OpenAPI subset, 66 model entries and 43 service presets.

## What this site contains

The full operating manual, agent instructions, all feature runbooks and their observed UI controls, API guide and discovered call catalog, model/service catalogs, verified schemas, maintenance procedure, verification register and demo findings. The [downloadable documentation package](downloads/veluro-documentation.zip) includes these materials and this searchable reader. Agents can begin with [llms.txt](llms.txt) and use [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt) for the combined Markdown reference.

## Private evidence archive

The original complete 98-file portable package and the six consolidated project-source documents are stored privately in the owner's here.now Drive. They include the complete meeting transcript, raw account-specific UI/API observations, draft tests, source attribution and reader screenshots. The raw evidence files are not public website assets. Source filenames and offsets in the published references remain historical citations to that private archive.

The website replaces account-specific record identifiers with placeholders. Credentials and session tokens are excluded from both editions. Model slugs, UI field names, documented procedures and evidence labels are retained.

## Verification boundary

Direct preflight/catalog reads comprised 26 checks, of which 25 returned 200 and one unsupported GET returned 405. Two controlled local draft lifecycles were completed and cleaned up. A name-only campaign update preserved structured copy; replaying the full creation body changed its representation.

Read [the verification register](VERIFICATION.md) before operating. Live ads, outbound delivery, publishing, generated media, provider connections, production optimization and multi-client isolation have not been certified by this baseline. A source-observed API entry is not a vendor-supported API contract.


========== MAINTENANCE.md ==========

# Keeping the Veluro agent current

This is the update procedure for a future recurring operator. No recurring automation was created during this documentation milestone.

## Before every material operation

Check account identity, plan entitlements, the relevant integration, feature flags and the live page. Compare visible buttons, labels and required fields with the saved runbook. Fetch current model slugs/prices for creative generation and current allowance balances for batch work. If the route or payload changed, refresh the evidence before writing.

## Daily review procedure

1. Open Home, Help, Settings → Integrations, Billing and the modules used by active clients.
2. Inspect meaningful new notices, provider gates, errors, quotas and feature additions. Do not mark notifications read just to inspect them unless the operating scope includes that change.
3. Compare the current client build identifier and discovered module routes with the prior dated snapshot. A changed build is a signal to inspect, not proof that every workflow changed.
4. Review active/pending jobs using stored IDs. Check known failure conditions, including the health-data provenance issue, before using recommendations.
5. Refresh any changed instructions and label their evidence level. Keep the old version for rollback.
6. Notify the responsible operator only for material changes, failures, completed checks or a decision that is actually needed. Do not issue repetitive unchanged status reports.

## Weekly deeper review

Re-read the relevant built-in help and vendor release information visible in the product. Compare plan grids and quota endpoints, shipping UI labels and prior demo promises. Audit new feature claims against actual controls and backend responses. Check whether a previously Coming Soon or approval-gated feature has become usable.

Use this order of evidence: independently verified operation and resulting state; current authenticated API/UI; current vendor documentation; dated demo; inferred behavior. A more recent source can still be wrong. Preserve conflicts rather than overwrite them silently.

The current terms and the absence of a public API support contract must be considered when deciding how to maintain production API integrations. Obtain the vendor-approved interface and change process for the service. Keep the internal source inventory as dated research evidence, not as assumed permission or a compatibility promise.

## Refresh records

For each changed feature, record:

```yaml
change_id: unique_reference
discovered_at: timestamp
feature: module_name
old_behavior: prior_verified_description
new_behavior: current_observation
source_url: exact_route_or_vendor_reference
evidence_files: local_references
evidence_level: tested_or_ui_or_source_or_vendor
affected_clients: client_ids
affected_runbooks: filenames
affected_api_operations: method_and_path
action_risk: read_draft_publish_send_spend_or_account_change
validation: completed_test_and_result
remaining_gap: precise_unverified_behavior
rollback: previous_working_procedure
```

## Change validation rules

For a label-only change, update locators and verify navigation. For request/response changes, first validate a safe read, then a reversible draft and read-back. For changes to launch, sending, billing, permissions, publishing or integrations, prepare the exact test and ensure the existing engagement authorizes its final action. Never mass-run every endpoint as a discovery test.

Do not replay a stale POST after a timeout. Resolve the current object/job state before retrying. Record the running job ID durably. Generation can continue after a browser closes; restarting blindly risks duplicate work and charges.

Maintain a small capability registry for each client with `available`, `connected`, `permission_scope`, `tested_at`, `evidence`, `limits` and `known_failure`. An account may have a feature label without permission to execute it.

## Agent learning and regressions

Keep approved business facts separate from platform procedures. Refresh platform procedures globally; preserve each client's business knowledge and permissions separately. Do not train client facts into another client's account.

After a meaningful platform change, evaluate the agent on: choosing the correct portal; selecting the correct client/account; recognizing a quota or integration gate; creating a local draft; interpreting a source-observed API operation; recognizing that LinkedIn Compose does not send; rejecting unexplained health metrics as business evidence; and recovering from an interrupted job without duplication. Preserve actual outputs and failures, not just a self-reported pass.

Archive each release with its dated manifest. Update the searchable HTML and Markdown together. Keep credentials out of every release and keep account-specific evidence private.


========== MANUAL.md ==========

# Veluro operating manual

Evidence date: September 8, 2026. This manual describes the authenticated Partner Growth account and the browser build `main.613ac379.js`. Use the [verification register](VERIFICATION.md) to distinguish tested behavior from a visible control or vendor description. Detailed screen inventories and instructions are in [Feature runbooks](runbooks/INDEX.md).

## 1. What the platform contains

Veluro combines business knowledge and an AI chat operator with customer acquisition, creative production, conversion and reporting tools. The authenticated application is at `https://veluro.ai`. The supplied login first enters the partner dashboard at `/partner`; its purple **Back to App** button enters the client application at `/home`. There was no second login in this account.

The partner portal manages referral tracking, recruited resellers, partner staff, promotional assets, commissions and payouts. The client application manages the business's operating work. Returning to the client app does not establish a separate workspace for every downstream customer. No tested multi-client switcher or isolation workflow was found in this account. Do not mix multiple clients' business knowledge, leads, mailboxes or budgets in one workspace without verifying the intended tenancy model.

The client sidebar is grouped into **Get Customers**, **Nurture & Close**, **Social Media & Creative Engine**, **Dashboard & Analytics**, and **Workspace**, with a separate Partner group. Groups can collapse. The search button says **Jump to…** and supports a displayed keyboard shortcut. The Home screen offers conversational tasks and feature shortcuts; direct routes and stable observed test IDs are included in each runbook.

## 2. Account, brand and business knowledge

Complete these foundations before generating a campaign:

1. **Settings → Profile:** verify name, business name, public contact email and optional phone. Login email is displayed as not editable there. Check the distinction between login email and the contact email printed on marketing materials. Save Profile and Save Changes are separate controls.
2. **Settings → Brand Kit:** select a logo, primary/secondary/accent colors and font. Add creative style instructions describing approved imagery, tone and exclusions. Save Brand Kit. The app lists Outfit, Inter, DM Sans, Manrope, Poppins, Playfair Display, Instrument Serif and Roboto.
3. **Workspace → Veluro Intelligence**, route `/teach-veluro`: teach the business using websites, uploaded documents and explicit notes. The UI accepts PDF, DOCX, PPTX, TXT, MD and CSV up to 30 MB. Note categories include company note, competitor, customer persona, FAQ, pricing and goal. Inspect the resulting knowledge list; uploading a document alone is not proof that all facts were understood.
4. Review the AI agent's memory in Settings. Treat automatically learned facts as editable, fallible memory. Keep credentials out of training data. Distinguish offer facts from exploratory ideas and unapproved prices.
5. Configure only the provider accounts assigned to the client. Verify the account/page IDs after authorization.

The current account reports `has_onboarded: true`, but High-Intent Buyers warns that the business description, industry and ideal customer are missing. “Onboarded” therefore does not prove a complete business profile.

## 3. Integrations and prerequisites

| Integration | What the screen supports | Current evidence / operator requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Meta Ads & Facebook Pages | Multiple ad accounts and pages; ads, custom audiences, social pages | Disconnected. Banner says the app is in Meta's final review and general one-click launch/auto-posting unlocks after approval. Verify current access before promising delivery. |
| Google Ads | Account authorization with `adwords` scope; Search / Performance Max described | Disconnected. UI says campaigns launch paused; verification is still in progress. Review the real authorization screen and provider state. |
| Google Analytics + Calendar | GA4 reporting and booking calendar sync | Disconnected. Verify correct property, calendar and timezone. |
| Google Analytics credential form | Measurement ID and API Secret | Separate from the combined OAuth connection. Do not assume one configures the other. |
| LinkedIn identity | OpenID Connect | This connection alone does not prove ad or messaging capability. |
| LinkedIn Ads | Marketing API, Sponsored Content, analytics, Matched Audiences, company posting | UI labels it approved Development Tier; disconnected here. Validate the intended ad account and page. |
| TikTok Ads | Campaigns, video creatives and reporting | Disconnected. UI describes paused creation. Posting is also a separate surface. |
| Email Outreach & Warmup | Gmail, Outlook and SMTP mailboxes | Live UI and client code expose these; actual delivery was not exercised. |
| Resend | Outreach and nurture delivery | Not connected. Outreach campaign tabs are gated until a usable sending route is connected. |
| SendGrid | Emails such as reports, notifications and outreach | Separate integration, with API key and sender email fields. Do not infer that it replaces Resend for nurture. |
| Twilio | SMS | Account SID, auth token and phone fields. Nurture says SMS stays queued until connected. |
| CRM connector | HubSpot, Pipedrive, GoHighLevel, Zoho or webhook | Two-way sync described. Validate direction, mapping, deduplication and delivery logs before client use. |
| GoHighLevel | Private Integration Token and Location ID | Help specifies contacts, opportunities, pipelines and calendars scopes. Use the specific sub-account's authorized token. |
| Bank / Financial | Provider and API key fields | Disconnected; data provenance and actual provider behavior remain unverified. |

The review did not connect third-party services, send support requests, change billing, or launch live work. Connection buttons may leave Veluro or open a new tab. They are authorization flows, not ordinary navigation.

## 4. Usage and the meaning of unlimited

The account's plan is `partner_growth`, displayed at $497/month in its partner plan grid. Its active billing subscription status is null and `has_billing` is false in the API; this establishes the entitlement label, not a verified charge.

| Meter | Verified allowance / state | How an operator uses it |
|---|---|---|
| General AI credits | 3,500 available; 0 used this cycle; rollover cap 10,500; renewal October 5 | Check `/credits` before costly batches. Purchased credits form a separate bank. |
| Creative Studio credits | 6,000 allowance; 0 used | Check `/omnirogue/usage` and model prices. These are separate from general AI credits. |
| Active campaigns | 5; 0 active | UI says drafts and paused campaigns do not consume a live slot. Draft test confirmed no active slot usage. |
| Intent leads | 75,000/month; 500 used; 74,500 remaining; reset October 1 | Check `/intent/quota`. Deleting a tracker does not immediately restore its allocation. |
| Landing pages | 3; 0 used | Check `/landing/quota`. Funnel accounting should not be assumed identical. |
| Social pages | 3 | Verify the actual connected pages and plan enforcement. |
| Coach seats | 1 | Billing says first use claims a seat; freeing a seat permits another person. |
| Coach analysis | 10 calls / 300 minutes; 0 used; renewal October 5 | This cap is additional to the seat limit. |
| Outreach mailboxes | 50; 0 connected; max daily cap 50 per mailbox | A maximum field is not an assurance of deliverability or an instruction to send at maximum. |
| Legacy media quota response | 300 images, 40 standard videos, 10 premium videos | The account also exposes Studio credits. Both counters exist; their interaction was not validated. |

Partner plan grid observed: Free $0; Starter $297; Growth $497; Command $997; Scale $2,497; Enterprise $6,497 monthly. Even the partner Enterprise grid shows finite general AI and Studio credits. Never translate “unlimited campaigns/leads/pages” into unlimited images, videos, mailboxes, people, labor or ad spend.

Customer retail pricing is a separate schedule:

| Customer plan | Monthly price | Campaigns | Intent leads | Studio credits |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Starter | $497 | 3 | 50,000 | 4,000 |
| Growth | $1,197 | 5 | 150,000 | 9,000 |
| Command | $2,497 | 15 | 500,000 | 20,000 |
| Scale | $4,997 | 25 | 750,000 | 40,000 |
| Enterprise | from $9,997 | Unlimited | Unlimited | 80,000 |

These are public retail figures, not this partner account's limits. The page advertises a seven-day trial. [Veluro pricing](https://veluro.ai/pricing).

For the future service, the operational unit should be an approved client request with defined inputs, output and completion criteria. Maintain a queue, prioritize work, and measure credits and operator time. The coaching/Skool benefit is part of the proposed service; no native Skool integration was established. Agency servicing rights, client isolation, data redistribution rights and any volume agreement remain to be confirmed before packaging multi-client unlimited access.

## 5. Customer acquisition workflow

### High-Intent Buyers

Navigate to `/intent`. Choose **Business buyers**, **Consumers**, or **Advanced search**. The first two use buying topics; Advanced search is filter-only and must not be described as intent-qualified.

For intent tracking, search with at least three characters and select up to five relevant topics. Topic search returns a `topic_id`, label and matching metadata. For example, the observed B2C roofing search returns broad roofing, specific service categories and named businesses; operators must choose semantic relevance rather than select the first result. Null `person_count` is unknown, not zero, and `match_score` describes topic matching, not purchase probability.

Apply geography using state, city and ZIP controls. A city search can return the same city name in several states: the Austin search returned multiple states, so explicitly select Austin, TX if that is intended. The visible signal recency field permits 1–14 days.

B2B filters include seniority, department, job title, LinkedIn connection counts, company size, revenue, industry, name and URL. B2C filters include age, gender, marital status, income, net worth, children and homeowner status. Apply only relevant and appropriate targeting criteria for the client's service and channel. The detailed runbook preserves the actual available options.

Name the tracker, set the lead allocation, review the summary and initiate it once. The UI currently defaults the allocation field to 25,000 and sets a minimum of 100; review this before using it. Creating a tracker can allocate quota. Poll the existing audience ID; the shipped UI polls about every six seconds until completion. Inspect records, counts and filters before export or activation. Audience quality, match rates and delivery were not independently tested in this account.

The call describes advanced search as unlimited and outside intent quota. The live screen's advanced-search notice should be checked at execution time; no bulk extraction was used to test quota accounting. Intent is a prioritization signal, not a complete census or a guaranteed buyer list.

### Demand Map

Choose the actual operating area and the products/services to analyze. Optionally choose a saved high-intent audience. Generate a map, inspect hotspots and selected location, then review any campaign it prepares. The observed request supplies `location`, `industries`, audience name and descriptive audience context; it does not establish deterministic person-level matching between every hotspot and the saved audience. Treat lead-volume and revenue estimates as model outputs until traced to a verifiable data source.

### Growth Engine

`/service-brain` assembles ads, landing content, outreach, booking and lead scoring around an industry/service/market/goal. The catalog currently has nine industry groups and 43 named services, plus custom inputs in the client code. The source-observed create request is `industry`, `service`, `market`, `goal`, `notes`. Capture the returned engine ID and poll it; inspect every component before launch. A launch payload includes `generate_images` and `publish_landing`, so launch can create media and publish a page rather than merely save text. Multi-service selection creates multiple engines and can multiply resource use.

### Manual ad campaign builder

Open **Campaigns → New Campaign → I know what I'm doing — open the manual builder**. The guided path checks platform connections first. The manual path has seven steps:

1. **Platform:** Meta, Google, LinkedIn or TikTok.
2. **Campaign:** objective, name and destination. Meta lead generation offers platform lead form or destination landing page. The common objectives displayed are leads, traffic, conversions and brand awareness.
3. **Audience / Google keywords:** choose AI recommendations, high-intent, a saved audience or broad targeting. Inspect geography. Google exposes exact, phrase and negative keywords; check terms and match types manually.
4. **Budget:** monthly budget, auto-optimization and maximum increase per adjustment. The draft's daily budget is derived from monthly budget divided by 30 and rounded. The default review showed auto-optimization enabled with a $100 maximum increase; turn it off or replace it with authorized settings before launch.
5. **Creative:** assets, primary text, headline, description, CTA and variations. Meta permits up to ten creatives in this UI, four additional primary texts, four additional headlines and two additional descriptions. Lead forms include intro, prefill/custom questions, privacy link and thank-you screen. A privacy URL is required for the Meta form.
6. **Simulate:** generates a prediction. It is not measured performance, proof of conversion or a guarantee.
7. **Review:** check full content, account/page identity, destination, budget, optimization, pixel and nurture sequence. A quality score may recommend changes; it does not replace launch validation.

**Save & finish later** preserves a local draft. **Save Draft** does not push an ad to Meta. **Save as Paused on Meta** creates provider objects in a paused state. **Make it Live** is a live advertising action. Source code also exposes platform-specific launch, pause, duplicate and optimizer operations; their contracts appear in the API catalog. For all providers, verify provider IDs and actual provider state rather than infer from the local campaign label.

A controlled UI/API test proved local draft create/read/update/delete, with auto-optimization false and no linked account, creatives, pixel or nurture. It used no credits or spend. The temporary draft was removed and the campaign total returned to zero.

## 6. Conversion and fulfillment workflow

Build the destination before directing traffic. **Funnels** provide multi-step flows, AI creation and templates; the editor source exposes page editing, step order, variants, automations, webhooks, payment connection and optimization. **Landing Pages** offer single-page generation, design inspiration, editing, assets, A/B variants, publishing and custom-domain controls. Generated copy and preview do not prove a served page, payment or conversion works.

**Pixels** support Meta, Google, LinkedIn, TikTok and custom script choices. Establish the provider pixel/tag ID, generate the install code, place it in the intended site or funnel, and verify events in the actual provider after an authorized test. A pixel listed in Veluro is not proof of correct installation.

**Chat Widgets** require bot identity, welcome message, goal, tone and business knowledge. Train using websites, files or notes. Test representative questions and lead capture before embedding. Inspect the generated snippet, placement, source domain and CRM destination. Do not let the bot invent policies, offers or availability.

**Leads CRM** supplies filtering, table/pipeline view, campaign grouping, scoring, import, manual creation, Meta lead sync and delivery log. Manual entry requires contactability by email or phone. A successful CSV upload is followed by header mapping, row/error checks and deduplication; validate against the original authorized list. Do not enroll people merely because they exist in the CRM.

**Nurture Campaigns** show sequences, statuses and enrolled leads. Email and SMS connection banners are separate. The activation action in this build is named `activate-send`; it is a delivery action. Review channels, timing, copy and stop conditions before activation. Funnel automation tests can send actual email/SMS; “test” is not synonymous with no external effect.

**Outreach (CSV)** handles lists, AI-created email sequences, replies and sender setup. It describes automatic routing through Resend when available, otherwise connected mailboxes. The current campaign tabs are disabled until delivery setup exists. The request supports list ID, purpose, value proposition, tone, sequence length, CTA and route choice. Verify the selected route against the intended sender, reputation and audience before sending.

**Email Triage** is a separate inbox/account workflow; **Replies Inbox** aggregates lead replies; **AI Reply Drafter** can prepare text from an email. Avoid reading unrelated inboxes. Copying or generating a draft is distinct from sending it. **LinkedIn Compose** explicitly generates copy for manual sending; the queue stores day-stamped reminders and status bookkeeping.

**Scheduling** manages dates, available slots, duration and linked contacts. Verify calendar selection, timezone, availability, conflict checks and event destinations. The public booking flow and calendar sync need production tests after connection. **Proposals** distinguish draft/save/PDF from sending for signature. **Sales Coach** separates prep, armed live capture and post-call review; the review meter exposes both calls and minutes.

## 7. Creative, organic growth and reporting

Creative Studio includes Guided, Pro mode, Photos → Video, Ad Lab and Storyboard Builder. Pro mode exposes video, image, avatar and voice/audio categories, though the returned model catalog currently contains image/video entries only. Use current model slugs and prices. Duplicate model names represent different variants. The captured catalog contains 66 entries; generation itself has not been certified.

Photos → Video says it joins 2–10 images with captions and transitions at no AI-credit cost. Ad Lab includes one-click ad assembly, template rendering, silence trimming and copy generation. Storyboard starts with script, duration and aspect ratio, then creates scenes/clips and stitches them. Store all job/project IDs and poll existing work before retrying. Review finished media for text, brand, facts, likeness rights and audio before client use.

Creative Library stores generated and uploaded assets, folders and video editing. Creative Insights needs a connected Meta account and should be assessed against actual ad data. Flyers expose text, business contact information, offer, CTA, QR destination, design choice, PDF download and image import. Validate QR and phone/website details in the exported artifact.

Social Media combines manual posts, AI strategy, batch queue and autopilot. Connect the correct profile, review generated content, set schedule and timezone, then authorize publication. Dragging calendar posts can reschedule saved work. Treat “approve and schedule” as a write that may lead to publishing. Provider approval gates remain relevant.

SEO Engine provides site audit, recommended changes, keywords and ranking tools; Blog Engine generates articles and publishes to the business blog. GEO exposes buyer prompts, scans, site audit, llms.txt and FAQ schema. These tools generate candidates for review; neither a GEO score nor a generated file guarantees rankings or AI recommendations. **Local Listings is Coming Soon** in both UI and help.

Dashboard separates Overview, Analytics, Command Center and Reports. Weekly Digest and reports can generate summaries, export PDFs and send email. Check date range, timezone, currency, source account and attribution definitions. Empty or disconnected source data must never be converted into a claimed result.

Business Health's populated account data is currently unexplained. Its API returned $220,602 monthly revenue, performance trends and budget recommendations while ad connections were false and total campaigns zero; the account's `demo_account` flag is false. This is a provenance conflict, not evidence of those business results. Do not execute health actions until the source is established. Some UI captures remained on “Calculating Business Health”; the separate API read succeeded.

## 8. Partner operation

The current links are:

- Public introduction: `https://veluro.ai/usingaitoscale`
- Direct signup: `https://veluro.ai/signup?ref=JUSTIN`
- Recruit resellers: `https://veluro.ai/resellpartners?ref=JUSTIN`

The portal describes 90-day visitor tracking and recurring customer attribution. Commission clearing is shown as 30 days; payout timing is the first of the month after clearing. These are portal terms observed, not a completed payout test.

The account's rates are 20% of direct referred customer payments; 10% of recruited reseller subscriptions; 5% override on reseller client revenue. The September 8 call states the same three-part structure. Account **My Team** means recruited resellers; **Team Members** means people working in the partner account. Partner staff permissions include earnings, marketing materials and campaigns, while bank/payout settings remain with the owner. The client app's **Team** page has a different Owner/Admin/Member permission matrix.

Starter Kit includes a personalized one-pager, share link, social copy, objection practice, objection cards and email templates. Marketing Library adds promotional assets and prebuilt campaigns with asset attribution. Treat templates and statistics as material to fact-check, not as automatically substantiated marketing claims. In particular, the proposed “every person in your area” claim goes beyond the evidence gathered here.

## 9. Operating cadence

For each new engagement, establish the client record and delivery chain before launch. Each operating day: check connections and allowances, failures and queued jobs, spending against approved limits, lead replies and suppression, and scheduled content. Check source-data freshness before following any recommendation.

Each week: reconcile CRM outcomes with ad and delivery data; report qualified leads, bookings and actual sales rather than only impressions; review creative fatigue and unsuccessful steps; refresh the knowledge base; track outstanding client requests and operator capacity. Prepare proposed changes with their expected effect and evidence, then execute changes already within the engagement's authorization.

Use the agent checklist and checkpoint format in [Agent instructions](AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS.md). Use [Maintenance](MAINTENANCE.md) for continuing platform expertise. This documentation does not itself deploy or schedule an autonomous operator.

## 10. Terms and documentation limits

Veluro's current terms disclaim guaranteed marketing and intent-data outcomes, assign responsibility for data and campaign decisions to the user, and prohibit misuse and reverse engineering. They do not establish a public developer API support contract or the multi-client/data-resale rights needed for the proposed service. Confirm approved automation access and service licensing before relying on the discovered internal interface as a production integration. [Veluro terms](https://veluro.ai/terms).

The API catalog is evidence of the app build and the controlled tests described here. It is not a vendor-issued OpenAPI specification, a promise of backward compatibility, or certification of every endpoint. The manual preserves these limits so an agent can operate accurately and improve the evidence over time.


========== README.md ==========

# Veluro operating knowledge base

**Milestone 1 — platform documentation and agent operating instructions**  
Research date: September 8, 2026 · Account reviewed: Using AI To Scale / Partner Growth.

This published documentation edition combines the supplied demo, the authenticated partner and client interfaces, built-in help, the browser-delivered application code, and direct API checks. Synced project sources were not changed. Credentials are intentionally excluded.

## Start here

- [Searchable manual](index.html): the searchable reader, including search across individual API call entries.
- [Operating manual](MANUAL.md): platform architecture, account setup, campaign operation, service boundaries, and known limitations.
- [Agent instructions](AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS.md): the operating contract for a future platform agent.
- [Feature runbooks](runbooks/INDEX.md): when, how, prerequisites, success checks, and recovery for each module; includes observed field and control inventories.
- [API guide](api/API_GUIDE.md): authentication, tested campaign operations, request and response behavior, and a complete catalog of the API call shapes found in this app build.
- [Verification register](VERIFICATION.md): proven behavior, conflicts, blocked flows, and remaining production checks.
- [Maintenance protocol](MAINTENANCE.md): how an agent keeps this knowledge current.
- [Demo findings](DEMO_FINDINGS.md): call evidence and changes since the demonstration.
- [Evidence index](EVIDENCE_INDEX.md): retained observations, test results and packaging boundaries.

The searchable edition is `index.html`. It includes 42 feature runbooks and 662 individually searchable source-observed API call templates. The Markdown and JSON files are the machine-readable source of that edition. The API subset documents 28 paths; the larger catalog is not a claim that every operation was tested.

## Read the evidence labels

**Tested** means executed and checked in this account. **UI observed** means a screen or control was inspected, but its final effect may not have been exercised. **Source observed** means the shipped browser code contains the behavior; it is not a backend guarantee. **Vendor described** means the help or demo describes it. **Unverified / gated** means production behavior could not be established here.

The documentation baseline is comprehensive across the discovered client modules. Production certification is still open for live advertising, outbound delivery, account connections, generated media, public publishing, and unattended optimization. These flows require real connected services and appropriate campaign scope. No documentation claim treats an unexecuted flow as tested.

## Important findings

1. Direct referral commission is 20%. The account's reseller terms show **10% of a recruited reseller's subscription plus 5% of their client revenue**. The demo confirms that distinction.
2. Partner Growth has finite allowances. “Unlimited service” needs to mean an operating offer within the client's purchased limits and approved external costs, rather than unlimited platform consumption.
3. Meta's integrations screen says general one-click ad launching and auto-posting await app review. Local Listings is Coming Soon. LinkedIn Compose is manual-send copy.
4. Business Health returned substantial revenue and campaign figures despite this account having no connected ad or financial services and zero campaigns. Treat those values as untrusted until their origins are reconciled.
5. The app's internal authenticated API works. A draft was created in the UI, read and updated through the API, confirmed in the UI, and deleted. No ad was launched; no AI credit was consumed. A published, versioned developer API contract was not located.

The complete original evidence archive is retained privately in the owner's here.now Drive. This site publishes the operating documentation, runbooks and API references; it excludes raw account records, the full meeting transcript, authentication credentials and original private downloads.

For another agent, start with [llms.txt](llms.txt). Download the [documentation package](downloads/veluro-documentation.zip).

Evidence date: September 8, 2026. This register is the source of truth for what was actually demonstrated.

The initial test draft was deleted; its historic identifier is retained in the private evidence archive. The second minimal-update test's draft was also deleted. Neither historic ID may be used as a production example ID.

## Material conflicts and gates

| ID | Finding | Implication | Resolution needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| V01 | User's proposed second-tier rate was 10%; account and demo distinguish 10% reseller subscription + 5% reseller client revenue | Commission forecasting needs three revenue bases | Use exact account terms; confirm agreement before public promises |
| V02 | Partner Growth quotas differ from public customer Growth pricing/allowances | Partner pricing is not customer pricing | Read the correct plan before quoting or provisioning |
| V03 | AI credits, Studio credits and legacy media counters coexist | One “unlimited” or “credits” figure is insufficient | Meter all applicable resources; validate how media counters interact |
| V04 | Intent credits reset October 1, while general AI/coaching show October 5 | Counters have different cycles | Store each renewal independently |
| V05 | Meta settings banner says final app review is pending | General launch and auto-posting access is gated | Re-check banner and actual account readiness before live delivery |
| V06 | Google verification banner remains; LinkedIn identity and Ads connections have different capabilities | A generic connected badge is not enough | Verify scope, account ID and provider's available operations |
| V07 | Local Listings says Coming Soon in UI and help | It is not a currently operable service here | Keep unavailable until the real workflow works |
| V08 | LinkedIn Compose explicitly never auto-sends | Drafting and reminders are available; automated DM delivery is not proved | Describe the workflow accurately; verify any future sending feature independently |
| V09 | Demo requested alternate SMTP; current UI and source now expose Gmail/Outlook/SMTP | Demo is not the freshest feature inventory | Retain current UI instructions; validate mailbox setup and delivery when authorized |
| V10 | Outreach lists/campaign tabs are disabled until sender setup | Downstream UI was not accessible with current connections | Use source-observed contract as provisional; verify after a client sender is connected |
| V11 | Consumer free trial reportedly lacked intent access; founder agreed to investigate | “All features for seven days” remains unproven for new customer accounts | Validate a properly scoped customer trial before leading with this claim |
| V12 | Health API returns populated financial/performance figures with no connected source and 0 campaigns; `demo_account:false` | Recommendations cannot safely be treated as actual business intelligence | Establish data provenance and reconcile metrics before any autonomous action |
| V13 | Transient 5xx errors and a temporary login redirect occurred; later reads succeeded | Empty/loading screens are not evidence of absent records/features | Use bounded retry and independent read-back; record failures |
| V14 | `/api/leads/statuses` was observed returning 404 during UI load | Custom-status operation is not fully validated | Test in a controlled client workspace before depending on custom pipelines |
| V15 | Common OpenAPI/docs URLs did not provide a schema: `/api/openapi.json` and `/api/docs` 404; root equivalents 403 | No public versioned API contract located | Establish vendor-approved API/automation access, support and change policy |
| V16 | Growth/partner workspace was inspected; multi-client tenancy was not proved | Partner referral visibility is not proof of isolated managed client workspaces | Validate account model, licensing and cross-client isolation before service scale |
| V17 | Demand map request uses location, industries and descriptive audience context | A saved audience selector alone does not prove person-level geographical targeting | Verify actual provider audience IDs, seed contents and targeting before launch |
| V18 | Some guide labels are stale: “New Audience,” old sidebar group names, and guidance to choose 3–6 topics | Built-in help can disagree with the live interface | Prefer current Track Intent UI and its five-topic limit |
| V19 | Model catalog has repeated display names and multiple prices | Name-only model selection can misprice a job | Use model slug + current cost/variant |
| V20 | Studio Pro exposes avatar/audio categories; current model API returned only image/video categories | Visible category labels are not proof that a usable model exists | Check live availability and validate output |
| V21 | Replaying a campaign create payload in PUT changed `ad_copy` from an object to a string and stored `ad_copy_details` separately | A successful rename can also alter the copy representation | Name-only PUT was independently tested and preserved copy; use minimal verified updates and compare the whole read-back |
| V22 | Google wizard's destination checklist can label its URL optional | Draft checklist completion does not establish a valid search-ad destination | Require and verify the intended destination before a website/search launch |

No support message was sent; no approval was requested from another person. These are specific production validation items preserved for the next authorized operating stage, not instructions for the user to do research.

## Required production certification

Run these in the intended client's connected account and within its existing authorization. Use a designated internal recipient or test conversion where sending is authorized. Complete all preparation before seeking any missing final approval.

1. **Provider connections:** establish precise user/ad account/page/property/calendar scopes; verify reconnect and expiry behavior; verify isolation from other clients.
2. **Ads:** create one reviewed paused campaign on each purchased channel; confirm provider object IDs and settings; then test an authorized live campaign with explicit spend ceilings and a stop condition. Verify pause truly stops provider delivery.
3. **Intent:** build a narrowly scoped tracker; verify allocation, returned count, record quality, recency and geographical mapping; export and compare; verify audience activation/matching; verify deletion's next-cycle accounting. Do not assume 100% identity or buyer accuracy.
4. **Pages/funnels:** build, edit and preview; publish on the approved domain; verify mobile layout, actual form submission, CRM fields, booking, tracking and payment if used; verify unpublish and rollback.
5. **Mailboxes/outreach/nurture:** authenticate the intended sender; verify routing and inbound reply handling; test delivery logs, unsubscribe, bounce suppression, reply stop rules, timezones and duplication protection before enrollment.
6. **SMS:** verify the intended Twilio number and outbound authorization, delivery receipts and suppression before a nurture step goes active.
7. **Creative:** generate one approved sample at the selected model/cost, poll it to completion, verify output, credit delta, saved asset and download; test retries without duplicate charges.
8. **Social:** prepare and approve one scheduled post for the intended profile; verify provider publish result; test rescheduling/canceling without duplicates.
9. **CRM/calendar:** validate import and field mapping, deduplication, sync direction, meeting timezone, conflict handling and public reschedule/cancel.
10. **Coaching:** validate live capture, file upload and review within agreed recording permissions; reconcile seat/call/minute accounting.
11. **Reporting/optimization:** reconcile all metrics to actual source events. Only then enable permitted optimization; verify maximum changes and audit trail. Health provenance is a blocking condition for health-driven actions.
12. **Partner:** test attribution using a controlled properly authorized signup, not an invented referral; reconcile settled commission and a real payout when available. Do not create synthetic business purchases to manufacture a payout test.

## Release position

This is a documented operating baseline and a tested local-draft API integration. It is ready to train an agent to navigate, prepare work, recognize prerequisites and verify operations. It is not yet a certification that an unattended agent can deliver every advertised live service. The distinction should remain visible in both the knowledge base and the future service's operating process.


========== api/API_GUIDE.md ==========

# Veluro API operating guide

Evidence date: September 8, 2026. Base URL: `https://veluro.ai/api`.

The authenticated browser application uses an internal JSON API. Login and local campaign draft operations work in this account. No published, versioned developer specification, service-account authentication, official SDK, stable rate limit, webhook contract or API support policy was located. The material below documents observed behavior; it is not a vendor-issued contract. The account's terms and any approved agency/API arrangement still govern production use.

## Choose the right reference

| File | Purpose | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| [Observed OpenAPI subset](observed-openapi.json) | Machine-readable paths and inferred sample schemas for checked reads, login and campaign drafts | Specific operations observed; schemas are inferred, not exhaustive |
| [Endpoint catalog](ENDPOINT_CATALOG.md) / [JSON](endpoint-catalog.json) | All 662 normalized method/path templates found across 833 browser call sites | Source observed; not 662 tested endpoints |
| [Draft request](draft-example.json) | Complete body captured from the UI's Save & finish later action | Tested local-draft creation shape |
| [Model catalog](MODEL_CATALOG.md) / [JSON](model-catalog.json) | 66 image/video model entries, slugs and displayed credit costs | Catalog GET tested; generation untested |
| [Service catalog](../runbooks/SERVICE_CATALOG.md) / [JSON](service-catalog.json) | Nine industry groups and 43 service presets | Catalog GET tested |
| [Feature runbooks](../runbooks/INDEX.md) | The relevant UI procedure, prerequisites and verification for each API family | Per-operation evidence varies |

The catalog's `{parameter_1}` names represent dynamic expressions in the application. They do not establish the meaning, accepted type or encoding of a parameter. Some entries combine path and query templates; do not add these literally to an OpenAPI server. `request_expression` is a research annotation, not executable JSON. A value such as `e`, `a` or `void 0` means the payload must be resolved from the current UI flow. For GET calls, the expression can be an HTTP-client configuration object (`params`, `responseType`), not a request body. Duplicate expressions were consolidated, so template counts do not imply a count of independent backend capabilities.

## Authentication and identity

1. Sign in at `https://veluro.ai/login` using the authorized account's securely supplied credentials. Partner users enter the partner portal; Back to App opens the client application without another login.
2. The login request observed in the app is `POST /auth/login` with JSON `email` and `password`. The browser stores its session token under `auth_token` and sends `Authorization: Bearer <session token>`. This is a session bearer token, not a separately issued developer API key.
3. Use `GET /auth/me` to verify the user and plan context before doing work. A successful login alone does not establish the correct client's workspace or provider account.
4. Keep credentials and tokens in the execution environment's secret store. Do not write them in prompts, knowledge entries, screenshots, URLs, request logs or this documentation. When using computer use, preserve the authenticated session without exposing storage values.
5. Token expiry, refresh, revoke behavior, service-account support and per-token scopes are unverified. On 401, stop the dependent operation, reauthenticate through the supported flow and verify identity again. Do not repeatedly replay a write after a login redirect.

An isolated browser-context read can use the current token without returning it to the agent:

```javascript
const identity = await page.evaluate(async () => {
  const token = localStorage.getItem("auth_token");
  if (!token) throw new Error("No authenticated Veluro session");
  const response = await fetch("/api/auth/me", {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` }
  });
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Identity check failed: ${response.status}`);
  const user = await response.json();
  return { user_id: user.user_id, plan_level: user.plan_level };
});
```

That example is an implementation pattern for an authorized browser session. It does not establish vendor support for unattended API access.

## Preflight reads

All paths below use GET and returned HTTP 200 during this review unless stated otherwise. Save the read time and account ID with every operational decision.

| Paths | What the agent should establish |
|---|---|
| `/auth/me`, `/billing/plan` | Account identity, plan entitlement, billing and trial state separately |
| `/credits`, `/usage/quota` | General AI balance, plan caps and legacy feature counters |
| `/omnirogue/usage`, `/sales-coach/usage` | Studio and coaching allowance; do not substitute the general AI balance |
| `/platform/flags` | Current provider/service issue flags |
| `/ads/connections`, `/ads/readiness-summary`, `/ads/stats` | Provider availability, account readiness and campaign/spend totals |
| `/integrations`, `/outreach/connection`, `/outreach/mailboxes` | Actual CRM/sending integrations, mailbox capacity and sender state |
| `/intent/status`, `/intent/provider-status`, `/intent/quota` | Provider state and intent allocation/renewal; `audience_count` alone is not a verified client-owned audience count |
| `/landing/quota` | Existing landing page count and cap |
| `/service-brain/catalog` | Current service presets |
| `/omnirogue/models` | Exact available model variants and costs |
| `/sales-coach/playbooks` | Current selectable coaching playbooks |
| `/health-score`, `/health-insights`, `/health-actions` | Response availability only; this account's values have unresolved provenance and cannot authorize actions |

Two lookup calls were checked: `/intent/topics/search?q=roofing&scope=b2c` and `/intent/city-search?q=Austin`. Topic responses contain separate B2B/B2C arrays and identifiers; `match_score` is not a person's probability of buying. A null person count means unknown. City search returned several cities named Austin in different states; use the complete intended city/state. Encode actual search values with `URLSearchParams`.

`GET /ads/optimizer/settings` returned 405. That proves GET is unsupported there; it does not mean an optimizer is absent. Do not try a different write method merely to see whether it succeeds.

## Tested campaign lifecycle

The checked lifecycle is a local Veluro draft. It did not create an ad in Meta, Google, LinkedIn or TikTok.

| Step | Request | Observed result |
|---|---|---|
| Create through UI | `POST /ads/campaigns` with [draft-example.json](draft-example.json) | 200; returned a `campaign_id`, `status: draft`, zero metrics |
| Read | `GET /ads/campaigns/{campaign_id}` | 200; persisted campaign returned |
| Full-body update | `PUT /ads/campaigns/{campaign_id}` using the create body with a changed name | 200; name persisted, but the `ad_copy` representation changed |
| Minimal update | `PUT /ads/campaigns/{campaign_id}` with only `campaign_name` | Separate test returned 200; existing structured `ad_copy` was preserved |
| Delete own QA draft | `DELETE /ads/campaigns/{campaign_id}` | 200; `message: Campaign deleted` |
| Verify cleanup | GET the deleted ID; GET stats and credits | 404 for deleted draft; total campaigns 0, spend 0, general AI usage 0 |

Both test drafts were removed. Their historic IDs in evidence are not reusable examples. The minimal update test also created its own local draft directly through the API with nonempty test copy before updating and cleaning it up.

### Creation fields

The draft example is deliberately incomplete for live advertising. A permissive draft save does not prove that a provider will accept its values.

| Field | Observed request shape and operating rule |
|---|---|
| `platform` | `meta` in the test; the UI also offers Google, LinkedIn and TikTok. Validate each provider's actual supported workflow. |
| `campaign_name` | String; use a unique client/job name and clearly label test drafts. |
| `campaign_type` | `leads` tested; UI offers traffic, conversions and brand awareness as well. Do not infer provider enums from display labels. |
| `lead_method` | `lead_form` tested; the UI also offers destination URL. |
| `page_id`, `ad_account_id` | Null accepted for a local draft; live work needs verified provider identifiers. |
| `destination_url` | Null accepted for this lead-form draft. Validate the actual landing destination for a website/search campaign even if a wizard marks it optional. |
| `audience` | Object with `mode`, `selected`, `names`, `geo_locations`, `region`; empty values saved in the test. Their presence does not prove targeting or audience activation. |
| `budget_monthly`, `budget_daily` | Numeric 30 and 1 in the test. These were draft settings, not spend. The monthly-to-daily UI conversion should be inspected for every chosen budget. |
| `optimization_rules`, `auto_optimize` | `{auto:false}` and `false` in the test. Keep disabled until the client authorizes explicit limits and the optimization path is validated. |
| `ad_copy` | String in the creation request. Read/update behavior differs; see the warning below. |
| `ad_copy_details` | Object containing `primary_text`, `headline`, `description`, `cta` and plural variation arrays. `LEARN_MORE` was accepted in the draft. |
| `creative_assets`, `creative_urls` | Empty arrays accepted in the test. Finished assets and provider requirements must be checked before launch. |
| `pixel_id`, `nurture_sequence_id` | Null accepted; only attach the intended client's tested conversion/nurture object. |
| `keywords_exact`, `keywords_phrase`, `negative_keywords` | Arrays, empty in the Meta test. Google UI exposes all three match types. No keyword upload/launch was tested. |
| `lead_form` | Nested name, intro, privacy, thank-you fields and questions. `FULL_NAME` and `EMAIL` were stored. Empty privacy content is draft-only. |
| `status` | Explicitly `draft` in both tests. Never use a guessed status value to launch, pause or terminate provider ads. |

### Update behavior that needs special handling

Creation normalized `ad_copy` into an object containing the structured copy. Replaying the complete create request in a PUT changed `ad_copy` back to a string and stored `ad_copy_details` separately. The GET afterward retained that changed representation. A second controlled test established that a name-only PUT preserved the existing copy object and its contents.

For a name-only edit, send only the changed name:

```json
{ "campaign_name": "Approved client campaign name" }
```

Read back the entire campaign and compare the intended fields plus copy, budget, status and account IDs. This tested partial-update behavior applies to the campaign-name case. It does not prove all fields merge safely or that every PUT endpoint accepts partial bodies. Changing copy or nested objects needs a dedicated draft test first; prefer the current UI until that path is verified. Do not take a GET response and blindly submit it as a create or update body.

### Operational request pattern

For each write, save the client/job ID, intended changes, previous values, returned object ID and completion check. Set a timeout; a timeout does not establish that the write failed. Read the existing object before any retry. Server idempotency-key support was not found, so do not invent an `Idempotency-Key` guarantee. Avoid simultaneous edits to the same campaign; version/ETag conflict handling is unverified.

Draft deletion was tested only on the task's own identified drafts. It does not prove that deleting an active Veluro record stops a provider campaign. For live ads, verify an authorized pause at the provider before considering record deletion.

## API families and their operating relationships

| Family | Typical sequence | Evidence boundary |
|---|---|---|
| `/service-brain/*` | Read catalog → create engine → read engine → review/edit blueprint → launch selected components | Catalog read tested; create/launch may consume credits or publish |
| `/ads/*`, `/google-ads/*`, `/linkedin-marketing/*`, TikTok ads | Read readiness → prepare draft → validate targets/copy/creative/tracking → use the correct provider action → read provider status/performance | Local draft tested; provider launch/pause/optimization untested |
| `/intent/*` | Check quota/provider → resolve topics/geography → build audience → inspect records → review drafts → activate the authorized channel → read activation status | Lookups/quota tested; audience build, export and activation untested |
| Landing/funnels/pixels | Prepare site/form/event → preview → validate destination/integration → publish/install → test actual conversion | Entry UI and source observed; deployment and tracking not exercised |
| Leads/CRM/integrations | Read destination and mappings → import controlled authorized records → verify deduplication/sync → bulk operation | Current connection reads tested; import and sync untested |
| `/outreach/*`, nurture, email, replies | Connect sender → verify sender health → prepare list/sequence → review routing/schedule → launch only within scope → inspect delivery/replies/suppression | Sender-state reads tested; downstream UI gated by missing sender |
| `/omnirogue/*`, storyboard, media/editors | Read model/usage → submit one approved job → record job ID → poll existing job → inspect asset → reconcile credits | Catalog/usage reads tested; generation/rendering untested |
| Social | Connect exact profile → create/review post → schedule/publish → inspect provider result | UI/source observed; publishing untested and Meta gated |
| Scheduling/proposals/coaching/widgets | Prepare accurate content/config → verify appropriate destination/recipient → execute scoped action → read resulting object/event | Entry UI observed; consequential actions not performed |
| Health/analytics/reports | Read data → establish provenance and consistent window → calculate/report → review proposed action | Reads tested; current health data fails provenance check |
| Partner/referrals/team/billing | Read relationship/terms → prepare exact authorized change → save → verify attribution/member/billing record | Partner UI observed; no invitation, payout or billing change tested |

Launch, activate, approve, connect, sync, send and publish endpoints are distinct actions with different consequences. A source expression containing `override_readiness` is not authority to bypass readiness checks. Even a GET can initiate an OAuth redirect or export data; inspect purpose as well as HTTP method.

## Asynchronous jobs, pagination, files and webhooks

The UI and source expose long-running generation, engine creation and audience activation states. Exact global job statuses, polling intervals, retry ceilings and retention periods are not established. An agent should record the returned job/object ID, use that feature's observed status route, apply bounded backoff with jitter and stop at its job deadline while preserving the pending ID. “Queued” or an HTTP 200 acceptance response is not proof of a finished video, delivered message or active campaign.

There is no verified universal pagination contract. Use only the current route's observed query parameters and response cursor/page fields; test completeness and deduplication. Do not append guessed `page`, `limit` or `cursor` parameters and assume they worked.

Exports can return blobs rather than JSON; one source-observed example is `/intent/audiences/{id}/export-csv`. Uploads can use multipart data; a minified body variable does not describe the supported file fields. Inspect the current UI request and allowed types/size before implementing uploads. Keep exported contact data within the intended client's storage and retention scope.

Webhook signing, event schemas, retry policy and delivery guarantees were not established. Do not invent a webhook integration. Poll validated read endpoints or use supported UI notifications until a real contract is available.

## Errors and recovery

| Condition | Agent response |
|---|---|
| 401 / login redirect | Stop dependent work; reauthenticate; verify identity and reconcile any in-flight write. |
| 402 / quota message | Preserve draft/job state; check each relevant meter. Do not buy credits or change plans without existing authority. |
| 403 | Inspect account role, provider scope and availability. Do not bypass access restrictions. |
| 404 | Verify route and object/account identity. A deleted QA draft correctly returned 404; `/leads/statuses` also returned 404 and remains a feature gap. |
| 405 | Method unsupported; inspect the actual UI's method and purpose before considering a different request. |
| 409 / validation error | Read the response details and current object; repair the specific issue. Exact error envelopes are not standardized here. |
| 429 | Honor a provided `Retry-After`; back off and reduce concurrency. Published rate limits are unverified. |
| 5xx / timeout | Retry safe reads with bounded backoff. For writes, first find the existing object/job/provider state to avoid duplicate spending or delivery. |
| 200 with unexpected data | Verify schema, identity and provenance; do not treat transport success as business success. |

Some rows above are operator recovery policy, not error codes actually reproduced. The review directly observed transient 5xx, missing/forbidden documentation URLs, the unsupported GET, and the deleted-draft 404. See [verification](../VERIFICATION.md) for exact observed gaps and the [maintenance protocol](../MAINTENANCE.md) for change detection.

## Evidence and production boundary

The evidence files preserve checked responses and controlled draft operations: `api-read-verification.json`, `catalogue-api-reads.json`, `draft-ui-create-test.json`, `draft-api-update-test.json`, `draft-minimal-update-test.json` and `draft-cleanup-test.json`. The generated subset schema intentionally leaves empty-array element types and unseen/null value types open rather than inventing validators.

Before relying on a new write operation, prepare the intended result, establish authorization and prerequisites, perform a small appropriate test, verify its actual effect and update the runbook. Maintain the vendor/API support, multi-client isolation, live delivery and data-provenance items in the central verification register. This documentation supports that work; it does not erase those gaps.


========== api/ENDPOINT_CATALOG.md ==========

# Discovered API call catalog

Base: `https://veluro.ai/api`. Source observed; not a vendor-issued schema. Read [API guide](API_GUIDE.md) first.

Dynamic placeholders do not establish parameter types. Request expressions are the literal shapes found in the app and must be resolved against a current verified payload before use. Missing body fields mean unknown, not that no fields are required. Observed HTTP statuses prove only those read responses.
